# ALS SubZero: Technical Documentation

Built by Samin Sami.  
ALS stands for "Al Sami" (first 3 letters of Samin Yasar AL Sami).  
Repository: https://github.com/Saminsami73/als-subzero  
License: MIT

---

## 1. System Design

ALS SubZero stores files in transit across network cables rather than saving them on physical storage media. It brings the acoustic mercury delay-line concept from early computers (EDSAC 1949, UNIVAC 1953) to modern IP networks.

Total in-flight capacity is governed by the Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP):

$$\text{Capacity} = \text{Bandwidth} \times \text{RTT}$$

For instance, a 1 Gbps connection with 40 ms RTT holds about 5.0 MB in flight.

---

## 2. ALS1 Frame Format

Every frame has a 24-byte header packed in Big Endian:

| Offset | Type | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0..3 | char[4] | Magic | ASCII `ALS1` (`0x41 0x4C 0x53 0x31`) |
| 4..5 | uint16 | Inode ID | Virtual filesystem inode index |
| 6..7 | uint16 | Chunk Index | Block offset within the file |
| 8 | uint8 | FEC Group | Stripe group identifier |
| 9 | uint8 | Chunk in Group | Stripe position (0..K-1 data, K..K+M-1 parity) |
| 10 | uint8 | Flags | Bitmask (0x01 parity, 0x02 last chunk, 0x04 reconstructed) |
| 11 | uint8 | Reserved | Zero padding |
| 12..13 | uint16 | Sequence Number | Increments on every reflection hop |
| 14..15 | uint16 | Payload Length | Bytes in payload (0..4096) |
| 16..19 | uint32 | Checksum | Castagnoli CRC32C over header + payload |
| 20..23 | uint32 | Epoch | Transmission timestamp in microseconds |
| 24..End | bytes | Payload | Block data or parity bytes |

---

## 3. Cauchy Reed-Solomon Codec

To survive dropped packets, the engine uses Cauchy Reed-Solomon erasure coding over $GF(2^8)$:
- Irreducible polynomial: $P(x) = x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1$ ($0\text{x}11\text{D} = 285$)
- Default ratio: $K=4$ data chunks, $M=2$ parity chunks per stripe
- Generator matrix: Cauchy layout $a_{i,j} = \frac{1}{x_i \oplus y_j}$
- Any $K$ surviving chunks out of $K+M$ invert the submatrix via Gauss-Jordan elimination to reconstruct missing data with zero bit errors

---

## 4. Departure Rate Pacer

When round-trip times are small (e.g. sub-millisecond local LAN), re-injecting packets immediately causes packet storms and socket buffer exhaustion (`ENOBUFS`).

The pacer holds packets in a priority queue:
- Calculates elapsed time: $\Delta t = t_{\text{arrival}} - t_{\text{epoch}}$
- Schedules departure: $t_{\text{release}} = t_{\text{now}} + (T_{\text{target}} - \Delta t)$
- Enforces a minimum 100-microsecond gap between consecutive packet releases

---

## 5. Shell Commands

Launch via `python -m als_subzero.cli.main shell`:

```text
Available Commands:
  ls [path]               Show files in dir
  cd [path]               Change dir
  pwd                     Print current dir
  cat <path>              Dump file contents from wire
  write <path> <text>     Write text into in-flight file
  put <local> [remote]    Push local file into wire
  get <remote> [local]    Pull in-flight file to disk
  mkdir <path>            Make directory
  rm <path>               Delete file
  stat <path>             Show inode and chunk info
  tree [path]             Show directory tree
  status | telemetry      Show live telemetry & RTT
  bench [loops]           Run loop persistence test
  serve [port]            Start web UI / REST server (default 8080)
  exit | quit             Exit shell
```

---

## 6. Web Dashboard & REST API

Launch via `python -m als_subzero.cli.main serve --port 8080`:
- Interactive developer console at `http://localhost:8080/`
- Endpoints: `/api/v1/telemetry`, `/api/v1/fs/tree`, `/api/v1/fs/cat`, `/api/v1/fs/write`, `/api/v1/fs/mkdir`, `/api/v1/fs/rm`

---

## 7. Verification

```bash
# Unit tests (20 tests, zero external dependencies)
python tests/run_all.py

# Benchmark under packet loss (0%, 2%, 5%, 10%)
python scripts/run_benchmark.py
```
